verdict.rationale: Pipecat ships Pipecat Evals, its own built-in system for testing agent behavior. You describe a conversation and the expected behavior, and it runs against the real agent's pipeline, services and code. The official CLI exposes an `eval` command (confirmed by runtime probe), and a local dev runner provides a separate develop-and-test surface ahead of production telephony. missing for 10: detailed docs on eval depth (simulated-caller personas, scoring/assertion types, telephony-specific simulation), independent hands-on corroboration of running evals.

support.subject: As a developer, I can test agents with simulated conversations or evals before putting them on real phone calls

citations.quote: Pipecat Evals is the framework's built-in system for testing agent behavior. You describe a conversation and the behavior you expect, and Pipecat runs it against your real agent
Pipecat runs it against your real agent (the same pipeline, the same services, the same code) and tells you whether the expectation still holds.
